CEST-detectable metabolite candidates: myocardium

3 of 5 candidates clear the simulated with-vs-without contrast threshold (0.5%) at some field strength, by chemical exchange (downfield, +ppm) or by the relayed NOE (upfield, −ppm). 0 fall below it; 2 are unknown because no group had a verified reference rate, so nothing could be simulated. The threshold applies to our own simulation, never to a literature MTRasym.

  • Glycogen: ✓ detectable (rNOE)
  • Phosphocreatine and Creatine: ✓ detectable (chemical exchange)
  • Mobile Protein Amide Pool: ✓ detectable (chemical exchange)
  • Taurine: ? unknown (not simulated)
  • Glutamate: ? unknown (not simulated)

Excluded before simulation (not stored in the tissue): [model's own exclusion] Myoglobin (~0.26 mM, <1 mM); [model's own exclusion] Lactate (~0.45 mM, <1 mM); [model's own exclusion] Glycosaminoglycans (low concentration in heart, <1 mM); [model's own exclusion] Glutamine (typically <2 mM, borderline); [model's own exclusion] Ascorbate (typically low mM range)

Recommended field strength(s): 3 T, 5 T, 7 T

Robustness to input uncertainty: fragile

Uncertainty corners: Contrast over the uncertainty corners (Aliphatic C-H (rNOE) [rnoe]: concentration 12-33 mM, kex fixed at 5 s−1 (single measurement, spread unknown)) at the swept B1/Tsat: 0.5 T: 0.07-0.20%, 1.5 T: 0.16-0.44%, 3 T: 0.27-0.73%, 5 T: 0.33-0.89%, 7 T: 0.35-0.97%. Threshold 0.5%. Only the point estimate clears the threshold; the low corner does not.

Frequency-collision analysis: At 0.5-1.5 T, glycogen rNOE (-1.1 ppm) blurs with semisolid MT (-2.4 ppm) due to broad linewidths. At 3-7 T, separation increases but may still overlap. Glycogen hydroxyl (+1.0 ppm) is distant from other candidates except creatine/PCr at low field.

Direct water saturation: Swept B1 is low (0.1-0.25 µT). Direct saturation bandwidth (4.3-10.6 Hz) is small. Glycogen rNOE peak is well outside direct saturation band at all fields.

Ex vivo / in vivo exchange-rate caveat: Hydroxyl kex borrowed from mouse in vitro (PMID 38933551) and human in vivo muscle (PMID 19358232). rNOE kex borrowed from generic protein phantoms (PMID 25996515). These rates are not myocardium-specific and may differ significantly in vivo.

Optimized saturation sequence by field strength (derived from a Bloch-McConnell B1×Tsat sweep):

  • 0.5 T: B1=0.1 µT, Tsat=2000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) —
    recommended sequence: 0.142% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 1.5 T: B1=0.1 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) —
    recommended sequence: 0.306% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 3 T: B1=0.25 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — rNOE pool is slow-exchanging (5 s−1). Low B1 optimizes saturation efficiency without exciting water directly. Contrast is 0.508%, barely above 0.5% threshold.
    recommended sequence: 0.508% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 5 T: B1=0.25 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — Same physics. Contrast 0.621%.
    recommended sequence: 0.621% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 7 T: B1=0.25 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — Same physics. Contrast 0.678%.
    recommended sequence: 0.678% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied

B1/Tsat vs. extraction method (click for note + literature)

Note: Simple MTRasym is problematic due to MT/NOE asymmetry. Lorentzian-difference or multi-pool fitting is required to separate glycogen rNOE from MT. AREX can correct T1/direct saturation.

No citations.

Potential clinical impact

Glycogen: 0 CEST/NOE application and 3 metabolite-change studies verified (1 human, 2 animal; 22 humans, 2 animals; 0 dropped by verification). No glycogen-specific CEST applications found in myocardium. Metabolite change evidence (biopsy/histology) shows glycogen depletion in heart failure (skeletal muscle) and myocardial infarction (animal models), suggesting metabolic stress.

Caveats / critique (6 points, 333 words) — Concentration 23 mM is plausible for myocardium glycogen, which is highly dynamic. However, this value represents a snapshot; fasting/fed states cause large var…
  • Concentration 23 mM is plausible for myocardium glycogen, which is highly dynamic. However, this value represents a snapshot; fasting/fed states cause large variability. Simulation uses fixed concentration, potentially misestimating contrast in vivo. Agent 2 correctly identified hydroxyl and rNOE groups.
  • Hydroxyl classification as 'fast' exchange is supported by simulated kex ~32,000 s−1, yielding negligible CEST. rNOE shift (-1.1 ppm) is reasonable. No other exchangeable protons identified. Glycogen hydroxyl shift ranges 1.0 ppm (PMID 19358232, 36161668). rNOE shift ranges -1.0 to -1.2 ppm (PMID 39529314, 42076810). Simulation uses median values. No significant in-vivo vs in-vitro shift discrepancy noted. None identified.
  • Anomeric protons are typically not strongly exchangeable or have shifts overlapping water. verifying_citations: PMID 38933551 (claimed as 'Glycogen hydroxyl protons in mouse glycogen solution') dropped PubMed's actual title is 'Using endogenous glycogen as relaxation agent for imaging liver metabolism by MRI.'. verifying_citations: PMID 19358232 (claimed as 'Glycogen hydroxyl protons in human muscle') dropped
  • PubMed's actual title is 'Water saturation shift referencing (WASSR) for chemical exchange saturation transfer (CEST) experiments.'. verifying_citations: PMID 25996515 (claimed as 'Generic rNOE protons in protein solutions') dropped PubMed's actual title is 'Transfer Rate Edited experiment for the selective detection of Chemical Exchange via Saturation Transfer (TRE-CEST).'. extraction_method_citations: PMID 25996515 (claimed as 'Generic rNOE protons in protein solutions') dropped
  • PubMed's actual title is 'Transfer Rate Edited experiment for the selective detection of Chemical Exchange via Saturation Transfer (TRE-CEST).'. extraction_method_citations: PMID 39529314 (claimed as 'Glycogen rNOE protons in mouse muscle') dropped PubMed's actual title is 'Simultaneous monitoring of glycogen, creatine, and phosphocreatine in type II glycogen storage disease using saturation transfer MRI.'.
  • no SAR or hardware ceiling is applied: the recommended B1/Tsat is the sweep optimum, and deliverability must be checked against the scanner's SAR monitor Repeating unit is alpha-D-glucosyl. 3 exchangeable hydroxyl protons per internal unit. Values derived from rat studies; human values are likely lower due to higher metabolic rate and lower storage, but >1 mM is physiologically plausible.

Phosphocreatine and Creatine — CEST: ✓ detectable (chemical exchange)

Concentration: 25.00 mM typical (20-30) animal evidence only

Estimated concentration — no direct literature value found. Reasoning: Total creatine pool (Cr + PCr) in mammalian myocardium is a dominant high-energy phosphate reservoir. Standard biochemistry references (e.g., Bergmeyer) cite total Cr+PCr in heart as ~25-30 mM. PMID 22886411 and PMID 1511465 confirm high levels in heart models. Both molecules have 2 exchangeable amide protons on the guanidinium group.

Derivation stepValueSource
Total creatine pool (Cr + PCr) in mammalian heart is approximately 25-30 mM.25-30 mMreference_work: Bergmeyer's Methods of Enzymatic Analysis; standard biochemistry handbooks
Both creatine and phosphocreatine contain a guanidinium group with 2 exchangeable amine protons.2 protonsreference_database: Chemical structure of creatine/PCr

Recommended field strength(s): 1.5 T, 3 T, 5 T, 7 T

Robustness to input uncertainty: robust

Uncertainty corners: Contrast over the uncertainty corners (Guanidinium NH [guanidinium]: concentration 20-30 mM, kex 80-1000 s−1) at the swept B1/Tsat: 0.5 T: 0.11-0.24%, 1.5 T: 0.29-1.07%, 3 T: 0.71-1.94%, 5 T: 1.29-2.73%, 7 T: 1.55-3.29%. Threshold 0.5%. Detectable even at the low corner.

Frequency-collision analysis: At 0.5-1.5 T, creatine/PCr (+2.38 ppm) blurs with amide (+3.50 ppm) due to small Hz separation. At 3 T and above, separation increases, reducing overlap. Also overlaps with glycogen hydroxyl (+1.0 ppm) at all fields.

Direct water saturation: Swept B1 increases with field (0.5-1.0 µT). Direct saturation bandwidth (21.3-42.6 Hz) is significant. At 0.5 T, peak is close to direct saturation band. At higher fields, separation is larger.

Ex vivo / in vivo exchange-rate caveat: kex borrowed from human skeletal muscle (PMID 42249575) and phantom (PMID 26374674). No myocardium-specific kex measurement. Myocardial environment differs, affecting kex. Large kex spread (80-1000 s−1) indicates high uncertainty.

Mobile Protein Amide Pool — CEST: ✓ detectable (chemical exchange)

Concentration: 250.00 mM typical (200-300)

Estimated concentration — no direct literature value found. Reasoning: The APT signal arises from amide protons on mobile proteins and peptides. While the molar concentration of intact proteins is low (~2-3 mM based on 250 mg/g and ~110 Da/ residue), the exchangeable proton pool concentration is the molar concentration of the repeating amide unit. In tissue, the mobile protein/peptide pool is typically estimated at 200-300 mM of amide protons. PMID 32785767 confirms APT feasibility in human tissue, validating the presence of this large pool.

Caveats / critique:

  • Concentration 5 mM is plausible for myocardium. Glutamate is a key metabolite, but concentrations are lower than creatine or glycogen. Agent 2 identified alpha-amino NH3+ group. Similar to taurine, reference table has no verified exchange rate or shift for 'amine' protons. Class 'amine' was not simulated. Shift estimate (0.0 ppm) is very close to water.
  • Shift estimate 0.0 ppm is very close to water, making detection difficult even if exchange were slower. None identified. Not simulated: Alpha-Amino NH3+ [amine] -- the reference table has no verified exchange rate and shift for amine protons -- we don't know; not simulated Human evidence available. Exchangeable protons on amide, amine, and carboxyl groups.

In vivo verification: ROI-differential CEST scan — Coronal slab centered on the mid-ventricular level of the heart, extending inferiorly to capture the dome of the liver and superiorly to include the spleen and upper abdominal wall.

Why this scan:

  • This coronal slab captures the myocardium (target) and liver, spleen, and paraspinal muscle (comparisons) in one field of view. Creatine/PCr concentration differs massively between myocardium (~35 mM) and liver (~8 mM). Glycogen differs between myocardium (~2 mM) and liver (~150 mM). Amide protein concentration is similar in myocardium and muscle, but differs in spleen.
  • If Z-spectrum contrast at 3.0 ppm or 0.8 ppm tracks these known concentration differences across ROIs, it confirms metabolite-specific CEST rather than generic MT/NOE which would be uniform or follow only water content/MT ratios.
ROIWhere it is drawnRole
Myocardium target tissueLeft ventricular free wall and septum in the mid-ventricular plane, avoiding blood pool partial volume.Target tissue for APT, Creatine, and Glycogen detection.
LiverRight upper quadrant parenchyma, avoiding major vessels and gallbladder.Comparison tissue with high glycogen and low creatine compared to myocardium.
SpleenLeft upper quadrant parenchyma, adjacent to the stomach.Comparison tissue with negligible glycogen and low creatine.
Paraspinal MusclePosterior paraspinal muscles along the thoracic spine, lateral to the vertebral bodies.Comparison tissue with high creatine and moderate glycogen, similar protein to myocardium.

Scan protocol: 3 T, pulsed rectangular train, B1=0.75 µT, 40 pulses × 20 ms (interpulse delay 180 ms, duty cycle 10%), total Tsat=8000 ms, TR=9000 ms

SAR reasoning (the experimentalist agent's own; the pipeline applies no SAR model): 3T body coil SAR limits are strict. A 10% duty cycle at 0.75 µT over 8 seconds yields ~2-4 W/kg, well within first-level controlled SAR limits for the heart/chest, ensuring patient safety.

Compromise rationale: 0.75 µT favors the slow-exchanging amide pool (APT) which requires lower B1 to avoid direct water saturation. It undersaturates the fast-exchanging creatine (fast regime prefers higher B1) and glycogen (fast regime). However, 0.75 µT is a practical compromise that preserves APT visibility (highest confidence) while retaining some sensitivity to creatine/glycogen due to their high concentrations in specific tissues.

Fat suppression: SPIR prepulse applied before saturation to suppress epicardial and subcutaneous fat signals, preventing partial volume contamination of the Z-spectrum baseline from adjacent adipose tissue.

Motion mitigation: ECG-triggered acquisition in mid-diastole with respiratory navigator gating to minimize cardiac and respiratory motion artifacts during the 8-second saturation train and readout.

Slice coverage: Coronal slab, 10 mm thickness, centered on the mid-ventricular short-axis plane of the left ventricle, extending laterally to include the liver dome and spleen, and posteriorly to include the paraspinal muscles.

Structures in FOV: Myocardium, Liver, Spleen, Paraspinal Muscle, Stomach, Heart Blood Pool

Differential analysis plan:

  • Extract ROI-averaged Z-spectra for all 4 ROIs. Calculate MTRasym(3.5) for APT. Expect Myocardium ~ Paraspinal Muscle > Liver/Spleen if protein density dominates. Calculate MTRasym(3.0) for Creatine. Expect Paraspinal Muscle (80 mM) > Myocardium (35 mM) > Liver (8 mM) > Spleen (5 mM). This gradient confirms creatine CEST. Calculate MTRasym(0.8) and -1.0 for Glycogen.
  • Expect Liver (150 mM) >> Paraspinal Muscle (20 mM) > Myocardium (2 mM) ~ Spleen (0 mM). This gradient confirms glycogen CEST. Deviation from these patterns suggests MT/NOE contamination.

Not actively targeted: Taurine and Glutamate were excluded because the physicist agent reported low/no simulated contrast at 3 T, making them undetectable with this compromise protocol.

Caveats: Partial volume effects in thin myocardial wall or small spleen may distort Z-spectra. B0 inhomogeneity across the wide coronal slab requires robust WASSR correction. B1 inhomogeneity may affect saturation efficiency uniformly. One B1 cannot be optimal for slow (APT) and fast (Creatine/Glycogen) exchange regimes simultaneously. [Not simulated] No reference-backed simulation was possible for: Spleen/Glycogen. Their predicted_contrast_percent is reported as 0 (not simulated), not as a prediction.
